events.title: Henry VII Crowned King of England
events.description: Henry VII was crowned at Westminster Abbey a few weeks after winning the throne at the Battle of Bosworth Field. His coronation confirmed the end of the Wars of the Roses.
events.significance: It began the Tudor dynasty, which ruled England for 118 years and included Henry VIII and Elizabeth I.

events.title: Act of Supremacy Makes Henry VIII Head of the English Church
events.description: Parliament passed the Act of Supremacy. It declared the English monarch the supreme head of the Church of England, a title that had belonged to the Pope.
events.significance: The Act completed England's break with Rome and set the course of the English Reformation.

events.title: Orson Welles's 'War of the Worlds' Broadcast
events.description: On the eve of Halloween, Welles and his Mercury Theatre on the Air aired a radio adaptation of H.G. Wells's Martian-invasion novel. It was written as a series of realistic news bulletins, and some listeners mistook it for real news.
events.significance: The broadcast became a landmark in the history of radio and a lasting case study of how media can shape public perception.

events.title: Soviet Union Detonates the Tsar Bomba
events.description: Over the Novaya Zemlya archipelago in the Arctic, the Soviet Union tested the AN602 hydrogen bomb, known as the Tsar Bomba. It yielded about 50 megatons of TNT.
events.significance: It was the most powerful nuclear device ever detonated, and it highlighted the dangers of the Cold War arms race.

events.title: The Rumble in the Jungle
events.description: In Kinshasa, Zaire, Muhammad Ali challenged heavyweight champion George Foreman in one of the most famous boxing matches ever held.
events.significance: Ali regained the heavyweight title in a fight that became a defining moment in sports history.
